title: Two-by-two table: chi-square, Fisher's exact test and the odds ratio
summary: Tests and estimates the association in a two-by-two table, without the continuity correction two of the four languages apply without asking.
_unadjusted_on_purpose: This is the crude table. Nothing here adjusts for anything, so it estimates a causal contrast only where the exposure was randomised or the plan can defend exchangeability without covariates. Where adjustment is needed the entry to use is logistic regression or the modified Poisson model, not this one with a covariate bolted on.
_matched_data_must_not_come_here: A matched or paired 2x2 -- the same patients before and after, or cases matched to controls -- breaks the independence this test assumes. McNemar's test is the paired counterpart and conditional logistic regression the matched one.
pinned_defaults: R: correct = FALSE. chisq.test APPLIES YATES' CORRECTION TO ANY 2x2 BY DEFAULT.
Python: correction=False. scipy.stats.chi2_contingency does the same by default.
R and Python both default to the CORRECTED value and both switch it off: 49.90 uncorrected against 49.19 corrected on this fixture, with every expected count in the hundreds.

The odds ratio is computed FROM THE TABLE in every file. R's fisher.test returns the CONDITIONAL MLE and scipy's fisher_exact returns the SAMPLE odds ratio; two files each reporting 'the odds ratio from Fisher's test' would disagree, and it would look like a bug rather than two estimators.
